tool_summary: The low-level RPM package tool that yum/dnf ultimately call. Installs .rpm files directly, bypassing repository/signature checks that yum/dnf perform, and runs arbitrary %post/%postun scriptlets at install/remove time.
platform_notes: rpm is used across RHEL/CentOS/Fedora and other RPM-based distributions.

rules.description: The --nodeps, --noscripts, or --force flags override rpm's built-in safety checks, allowing installation despite dependency conflicts or file conflicts, or skipping/altering the execution of packaging scriptlets in ways that can leave the system in an inconsistent state.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but overwritten files and install-time scriptlet side effects may not be recoverable.

rules.description: Installs an .rpm package file directly. This bypasses yum/dnf's repository signature verification entirely, since rpm operates on a local file. Runs arbitrary %post scriptlets with root privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but install-time scriptlets may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The -e/--erase flag removes a package, running %preun/%postun scriptlets with root privileges.
Manages RPM packages at a low level. Read-only subcommands (-q, -qa, -qi) do not alter system state.
